title: Never Read Out the Six Digits

pages.text: For their Basic 9 Career Technology project, Pokuaa, Seyram, and Abdul-Aziz sewed African-print laptop sleeves and made keyholders from recycled-glass beads. Pokuaa measured each fabric panel with her tape measure and added a seam allowance of 1.5 cm all round. She cut with pinking shears, whose zigzag edge stops cotton from fraying, and pressed every seam flat. For PTA day, Seyram made a QR code. Any parent who scanned it with a phone would see the group’s price list, which could be read but not changed.

Pokuaa measured each fabric panel with her tape measure and added a seam allowance of 1.5 cm all round.
She cut with pinking shears, whose zigzag edge stops cotton from fraying, and pressed every seam flat.
For PTA day, Seyram made a QR code.
Any parent who scanned it with a phone would see the group’s price list, which could be read but not changed.
pages.alt: In the Career Technology sewing room, Pokuaa measures colourful African-print fabric with a 1.5 cm seam allowance while Seyram tests scanning a printed QR code poster with a school tablet.

pages.text: Parents ordered twelve laptop sleeves at GH¢ 50.00 each, GH¢ 600.00 in all. They paid into the club’s Mobile Money wallet, which Miss Tetteh supervised. Then the project phone rang. “This is Mobile Money head office!” a man said, speaking very fast. “A wrong reversal of GH¢ 600 is pending on your wallet. A six-digit code has just come to you by SMS. Read it to me now, or tap the link in our message. You have two minutes before your account is blocked!” Seyram froze. On the screen, a six-digit One-Time Password, an OTP, was flashing.

Then the project phone rang.

“A wrong reversal of GH¢ 600 is pending on your wallet.
A six-digit code has just come to you by SMS.
Read it to me now, or tap the link in our message.
You have two minutes before your account is blocked!” Seyram froze.
On the screen, a six-digit One-Time Password, an OTP, was flashing.
pages.alt: Close-up dramatic gouache scene of the club’s phone displaying an incoming call from an unknown ordinary number alongside an SMS warning: NEVER SHARE YOUR 6-DIGIT OTP WITH ANYONE.

pages.text: Pokuaa reached over and ended the call. Not one digit had been read out. “Well done,” said Miss Tetteh. She pointed to the Information Security chart on the wall. “Security rests on three things. Confidentiality: secrets stay secret. Integrity: records are not altered. Availability: systems work when you need them. That caller was attacking confidentiality. An OTP is a key, and he wanted you to hand it over. And the message with the link? That is phishing: a fake message made to trick you into giving up a secret. Do not trust a link just because it begins with https. Scammers use that too. No real provider will ever ask for your PIN or OTP.”

“Well done,” said Miss Tetteh.
She pointed to the Information Security chart on the wall.
“Security rests on three things.
Confidentiality: secrets stay secret.
Integrity: records are not altered.
Availability: systems work when you need them.
That caller was attacking confidentiality.
An OTP is a key, and he wanted you to hand it over.
And the message with the link?
That is phishing: a fake message made to trick you into giving up a secret.
Do not trust a link just because it begins with https.
Scammers use that too.
No real provider will ever ask for your PIN or OTP.”
pages.alt: Miss Tetteh points to an Information Security poster showing the CIA Triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability) and the four data threats on a classroom wall.

pages.text: Abdul-Aziz had spotted another weakness. Seyram wanted to set the tablet’s four-digit PIN to 2012, the year they were born. He opened his Mathematics exercise book. “Think about probability,” he said. “A thief who knows our ages will try birth years first. If there are four likely years, the first guess has a 1 in 4 chance. But a random four-digit PIN can be anything from 0000 to 9999. That is 10,000 possibilities, so one guess has a 1 in 10,000 chance. A six-digit code has a million possibilities. That is exactly why a scammer cannot guess an OTP. He has to trick you into telling him.”

pages.alt: Abdul-Aziz writing clean probability fractions on the board comparing a predictable birth-year PIN (1/4) vs a random 4-digit PIN (1/10,000) vs a 6-digit OTP (1/1,000,000).

pages.text: The group checked the wallet in the official app. No money had left. Then they balanced their records. One parent had bought four sleeves and earned a 5% bulk discount. Four sleeves at GH¢ 50 came to GH¢ 200, and 5% of GH¢ 200 is GH¢ 10, so she paid GH¢ 190. Total collections were therefore GH¢ 590, not GH¢ 600. The service charge was 1% of GH¢ 590, which is GH¢ 5.90. Abdul-Aziz checked every pesewa until the ledger matched the wallet. “That is integrity,” said Miss Tetteh. “Records you can trust.”

pages.text: Before closing, the group added a bright safety box beside the QR code on their banner. It read: “Never share your PIN or OTP with any caller or in any message. Do not open payment links you were not expecting. Check your balance only in the official app or with the official short code. Report suspicious calls to a trusted adult or to your provider.” Parents bought the last bead keyholders. Many also photographed the safety box to show their families. Good craft had earned the money. Clear thinking kept it safe.

activities.question: In Information Security, what are the three parts of the CIA triad?
The caller wanted Seyram to read out the OTP. Which part of the CIA triad was he attacking?
options: Confidentiality, because an OTP is a secret only its owner should know
Availability, because the tablet battery was low
Integrity, because the price list could not be edited

activities.question: Every digit of a random 4-digit PIN is 0 to 9 (10,000 combinations). What is the chance of guessing it in one attempt?

activities.prompt: Put the safe verification steps in order when you receive a suspicious payment-reversal call or SMS.
items: Pause—do NOT panic, click links, or read out any PIN or 6-digit OTP.
Hang up the suspicious call and inspect sender number carefully.
Check wallet balance independently using official shortcode or app.
Report and block fraudulent number through telecom fraud helpline.
